text.text:
Production is experiencing a P1 incident centered on `payment-service`: `DB_CONN_TIMEOUT` errors, PostgreSQL pool exhaustion on `postgres-primary` (`active_connections=195 max_connections=200` and `FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections`), `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`, and `CrashLoopBackOff/OOMKilled` restarts on pod `payment-service-7d9f84c9b6-rx2pm`.  
The impact extends to `postgres-primary`, `api-gateway`, `auth-service`, `redis-cache`, `kubelet`, `kubernetes`, and `deployment-controller`; `api-gateway` is returning 401s from auth timeouts, and `payment-service` availability is down to `1/6` replicas after the `v2.8.4` deployment.  
Overall severity is P1 with immediate user impact on payment transaction creation and authenticated API access, causing intermittent unavailability and elevated 401/timeout failures in production.  
The single most critical next step is to roll back `payment-service` from `v2.8.4` to `v2.8.3` immediately to stop the deployment from amplifying DB pressure and crash loops.

*Issues Identified:*
• *DB_TIMEOUT* on `payment-service, postgres-primary, api-gateway` — P1 (confidence: 99%)
• *OOM_KILL* on `payment-service, kubelet, kubernetes` — P1 (confidence: 99%)
• *DB_TIMEOUT* on `postgres-primary, payment-service` — P1 (confidence: 90%)
• *AUTH_ERROR* on `auth-service, redis-cache, api-gateway` — P1 (confidence: 97%)
• *DEPLOY_FAILURE* on `payment-service, deployment-controller, kubernetes` — P1 (confidence: 84%)
